habit.lifeForm.value: evergreen perennial twining herb, grown outdoors in Britain as an annual
habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: an "evergreen, perennial twining climber, often grown as an annual, to 2.5m tall". Weeds of Australia: "a perennial herbaceous climber".

habit.strainDrawn.value: the orange, dark-eyed form of the species
habit.strainDrawn.basis: The species is sold as seed strains in orange, yellow, cream and white, with and without the eye. The model draws the form the species was described from and the RHS describes first ("orange to yellow flowers with dark brown centres"), the one sold as 'Susie Orange with Black Eye'. A choice of which plant is planted, not a finding.

stem.twiningHandedness.basis: As in taxon.json. Darwin's table: Thunbergia alata "moves against the sun", which is anticlockwise seen from above when climbing, a right-handed helix (vocab.ts HANDEDNESS).

stem.section.basis: Wasshausen & Wood (2004), Acanthaceae of Bolivia: stem "subquadrate to flattened, pubescent". A description from Bolivian collections of a plant naturalised there; the species is the same.

stem.surface.value: green and slender, hairy when young
stem.surface.basis: Weeds of Australia: stems "slender and green, and hairy (pubescent) when young". Botany Brisbane adds that the base may become woody in older plants, which a plant of one British summer does not reach. Photographs show the older lengths of stem flushed a dull purplish brown (Commons: "Starr-110307-2322-Thunbergia alata-flowers and leaves-Kula Botanical Garden-Maui", "Thunbergia alata close.JPG"); the model colours them so.

stem.diameterM.basis: Two figures, neither traced to a flora that could be opened: "one to one and a quarter millimeter thick" in an encyclopedia article, and "slender (ca. 2 mm)" in a guide text. Recorded as a bracket, not as a measurement.

stem.internodeLengthM.basis: "Four and a half to 13 centimeters" between one pair of leaf stalks and the next, from an encyclopedia article that names no flora for it. The only figure found; unverified.

leaf.arrangement.basis: Weeds of Australia: leaves opposite. Darwin: "the opposite leaves of Thunbergia alata".

leaf.division.basis: North Carolina State Extension: leaf simple, opposite.

leaf.shape.basis: Weeds of Australia: "ovate or arrow-shaped (hastate or sagittate)". Wasshausen & Wood: "sagittate". RHS: "heart-shaped to oval". Wisconsin Extension: "oval to triangular or heart-shaped".

leaf.base.value: cordate-hastate, the two basal lobes pointing outwards, the blade running down the stalk as its wing
leaf.base.basis: Wasshausen & Wood: blade "cordate-hastate at base". Botany Brisbane: "outward-pointing basal lobes".

leaf.apex.value: acute to acuminate, often with a small point
leaf.apex.basis: Weeds of Australia: tips "acuminate, acute or mucronate".

leaf.margin.value: entire to shallowly and coarsely toothed, a little wavy
leaf.margin.basis: Weeds of Australia: "entire to toothed margins". RHS: "toothed leaves". Wisconsin Extension: "slightly toothed". Wasshausen & Wood: "entire to undulate".

leaf.teethPerSide.basis: No description counts them. Read from photographs: one to three blunt angles on each side, in the lower two thirds of the blade, more like the corners of an ivy leaf than the teeth of a saw (Commons: "Black eyed susan flower in london.jpg", "Black-eyed Susan 2.JPG", "Starr-110307-2322-Thunbergia alata-flowers and leaves-Kula Botanical Garden-Maui"); some leaves have none ("Mosca abeja.jpg").

leaf.basalVeins.basis: Read from photographs: five main veins spread from the top of the stalk, the outer pair running into the basal lobes, with sometimes a weaker pair beyond (Commons: "Mosca abeja.jpg", "Black eyed susan flower in london.jpg"). Wisconsin Extension says only "prominent veins" beneath. The Flora of China account could not be opened to check.

leaf.bladeLengthM.basis: Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: "leaf blades about 3-8 x 3-7.5 cm". Weeds of Australia: 2-8 cm long. Wasshausen & Wood: 2-13.5 cm. Wisconsin Extension: up to 3 inches.

leaf.bladeWidthM.basis: Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: "about 3-8 x 3-7.5 cm", measured across the basal lobes. Weeds of Australia gives a narrower leaf, 1-4.5 cm wide; Botany Brisbane up to about 8 x 5 cm.

leaf.widthToLength.basis: The blade's width for its length, between the ratios of the middles of two published ranges: 0.55 (Weeds of Australia, 2-8 x 1-4.5 cm) and 0.95 (Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants, 3-8 x 3-7.5 cm). Photographs show both ends on garden plants: a narrow toothed leaf (Commons: "Thunbergia alata close.JPG") and a leaf nearly as wide as long (Commons: "Black eyed susan flower in london.jpg"). The model draws leaves at three points within the range. Derived, not measured.

leaf.petioleLengthM.basis: Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: "petioles about 2.5-3.5 cm long". Weeds of Australia: 1.5-6 cm. Taken from the same source as the blade so that the two go together.

leaf.petioleWing.value: winged on both sides over much of its length, the wing widening towards the blade
leaf.petioleWing.basis: Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: petioles "distinctly winged over much of their length". Weeds of Australia: "narrowly winged". Botany Brisbane: wings on both sides, even in width or wider towards the top. It is what the name alata records.

leaf.petioleWingWidthM.basis: Across both wings, at the stem end and at the blade end of the stalk. No description gives a width. Read from a photograph in which the stalk shows as a flat green strap about 5 mm across below a blade about 8 cm long (Commons: "Black eyed susan flower in london.jpg"); in others the wing is too narrow to see.

leaf.surface.value: softly hairy on both sides, dull
leaf.surface.basis: Wisconsin Extension: "soft and hairy", "dull dark green above". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: both surfaces hairy.

leaf.colour.value: dull dark green above, pale green with prominent veins beneath
leaf.colour.basis: Wisconsin Extension: "dull dark green above, pale green with prominent veins below".

leaf.posture.value: the stalk spreading, the blade hanging from it tip downwards and facing outwards, the leaves lying over one another like tiles
leaf.posture.basis: Read from photographs of plants on walls and trellis (Commons: "Climber at timber-framed house, Limburg.jpg", "Black-eyed Susan 2.JPG", "Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg"): blades hang at 45 degrees and more from their stalks. The model cannot follow this beyond about 30 degrees (a leaf model must stay nine tenths of its length along its axis), and the engine sets leaves round the stem without regard to where the light is.

leaf.coldColour.basis: It has no autumn colour: it is evergreen where it is warm. What a British plant does as the cold takes it is not described in any source read; the yellowing and browning drawn are how tender foliage generally goes, and a guess for this plant.

flower.arrangement.value: solitary in the leaf axils, each on its own long stalk
flower.arrangement.basis: Weeds of Australia: "borne singly in the upper leaf forks". Wisconsin Extension: "borne singly in the leaf axils". Botany Brisbane: usually one to an axil, occasionally two.

flower.pedicelLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: "on pedicels 30-95 mm long". Botany Brisbane: hairy, up to 8 or 9 cm.

flower.bracteoleCount.basis: Weeds of Australia: "two leafy bracts" at the base of each flower, easily taken for sepals. Wisconsin Extension: "two large, ridged, hairy green bracts".

flower.bracteoleLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: bracts "12-20 mm long". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: about 15-20 x 15 mm. Wasshausen & Wood: 11-25 mm.

flower.bracteoleWidthM.basis: Wasshausen & Wood: bracteoles "green, lance-ovate to ovate, 11-25 x 4-15 mm, pubescent". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: about 15 mm wide.

flower.calyxLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: "the calyx is 2-3 mm long", a ring of tiny teeth hidden between the bracts.

flower.calyxLobeCount.basis: Weeds of Australia: "11-14 tiny sepals fused together". Wasshausen & Wood: "annular, 11-13 lobed". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: 10-12 awl-shaped lobes.

flower.widthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: flowers "3-4 cm wide". Wisconsin Extension: about 1 1/2 inches. This is what the growth model's organs.racemeLengthM measures for this plant, and the size the flower model is authored at.

flower.tubeLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: "the corolla tube is 15-25 mm long". Botany Brisbane: a narrow lower part of about 5 mm round the ovary and a wider upper part of about 2 cm, straight or curved.

flower.lobeCount.basis: Weeds of Australia: "five spreading lobes". RHS genus page: "five-petalled".

flower.lobeLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: lobes "10-15 mm" long.

flower.lobeShape.value: obovate to obdeltate, cut off square at the tip, overlapping, the limb opening flat
flower.lobeShape.basis: Wasshausen & Wood: "limb subactinomorphic; lobes obovate to obdeltate, apically truncate". Wisconsin Extension: "opens flat, with five overlapping petals". Singapore NParks: tips nearly flat with a small notch in the middle.

flower.lobeFreeShare.basis: How much of a lobe's length stands free of its neighbours, the rest being joined or overlapping. Read from photographs: free for a little under half in flowers whose lobes overlap ("Thunbergia alata 1DS-II 1-1742.jpg", "Thunbergia alata close.JPG"), for two thirds in flowers whose lobes stand apart like the blades of a propeller ("Black Eyed Susan (Thunbergia alata) with orange flowers.jpg", "Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg"). All on Commons. The model draws the middle.

flower.colour.basis: RHS: "orange to yellow flowers with dark brown centres". Wasshausen & Wood: "orange or yellow". Wisconsin Extension: "the usual type is brilliant orange". The orange form is the one drawn (habit.strainDrawn).

flower.eyeColour.basis: Wasshausen & Wood: "a dark purple glandular eye in the throat". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: throat "reddish brown to black", hairy. Wisconsin Extension: "brownish-maroon center". RHS: "dark brown centres".

flower.eyeShareOfWidth.basis: The dark eye as a share of the flower's width. Read from photographs on Commons: about a fifth ("Thunbergia alata, Hungary.jpg", "Black eyed susan flower in london.jpg", "Thunbergia alata 1DS-II 1-1742.jpg") to a quarter ("1024 Schwarzäugige Susanne-1858.jpg", "Black-eyed Susan 2.JPG"). With the published width it puts the lobes at 13 to 14 mm, inside the published 10-15 mm.

flower.reverseColour.value: the back of the lobes the same orange a little paler; the tube pale yellow orange outside
flower.reverseColour.basis: No description read gives it. Read from a photograph that shows flowers side on (Commons: "Black Eyed Susan (Thunbergia alata) with orange flowers.jpg"). The model draws a lobe in one colour on both faces.

flower.stamenCount.basis: Weeds of Australia: "four stamens". Botany Brisbane: in two slightly unequal pairs, the longer to 9 mm, set low in a tube 15-25 mm long, so that they and the style stay inside it and do not show.

fruit.kind.value: a hairy capsule with a round base and a long flattened beak, held in the two persistent bracts
fruit.kind.basis: Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: fruits "enclosed by two persistent bracts", "globular at the base", ending in "a laterally compressed beak". Wisconsin Extension: "a round base and a long beak, resembling a bird's head".

fruit.baseDiameterM.basis: Weeds of Australia: "a globular base 5-10 mm across". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: about 8 mm.

fruit.beakLengthM.basis: Weeds of Australia: "an elongated beak 9-15 mm long". Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: about 13 mm. Botany Brisbane: nearly 2 cm.

fruit.baseHeightToWidth.basis: The round base of the capsule is lower than it is wide, in two swellings with a furrow between. Read from one photograph of a ripening capsule (Commons: "Kapselfrucht.jpg"); Wasshausen & Wood call the capsule depressed-globose, which agrees. The same photograph shows the beak stouter than drawn at first, about a third as thick as the base is wide, and the bracts withered and hanging beneath a ripe capsule; a second ("Kapselfrucht 02.jpg") shows them green, folded and standing apart either side of the green beak, which is how the model draws them at every age.

fruit.colour.value: green, drying to tan and brown
fruit.colour.basis: Wisconsin Extension: the fruit, enclosed in the green bracts, "ripens and dries to tan". Weeds of Australia: "turns from green to brown as it matures".

seed.count.basis: Wisconsin Extension: "2 or 4 semicircular, reticulate seeds". Wasshausen & Wood: 2. Australian Tropical Rainforest Plants: usually 4, about 4 mm.
